prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: acceptance/transfer→screening/sorting/make-up→Outbound Load Control Desk; excludes airline loading. No explicit modes. Objectives: safety, association accuracy, throughput, cutoffs. Elements/items (recipients unspecified): Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit records acceptance/ID, initiates processing, sends Oversize Exception Ticket. Bag Tag Printer produces unique durable tags/Calibration Witness Tag. Flight Data Gateway (Lantern) supplies flight/routing data, sends Flight Cutoff Advisory. Transfer Bag Feeder records arrivals, sends Late Transfer Bag Card; holds until screening/onward handling confirmed. Concourse Zone Controller (Mosslight) coordinates equipment/conveyors with active plan/restrictions, produces Recovery Route Card. Induction Tray Conveyor separates/spaces bags for imaging/identification. North Gate Scanner (Kestrel)/South Gate Scanner independently identify respective entries/decision points, capture images/return dispositions; South produces Manual Rescan Receipt. Primary Crossbelt Sorter (Juniper) preserves identity, applies destination/screening status, sends Chute Occupancy Note near configured capacity. Image Resolution Desk staff resolve images using images/ID/prompts, record dispositions. Bag Reconciliation Station matches presented bag/ID/status to screening record. East Make-Up Conveyor/West Make-Up Conveyor convey; Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit (Orchard) stages only valid-disposition/authorized-route bags. Outbound Load Control Desk confirms readiness; Airline Ramp Coordinator coordinates acceptance, sends Carousel Release Slip upon build authorization. Baggage Control System (Velvet): links passenger/flight/ID, exchanges status/routing/restrictions, validates acceptance/transfer records, applies approved screening profiles; loads approved sort plan/effective window, checks current records, favors authorized capacity/time-sufficient routes; sends exceptions to Secondary Inspection Chute. Requirements: verify eligibility/size/weight/IDs; hold deficiencies/oversize. Induct only valid-record/available-route/ready-equipment; interlocks stop jams/open-doors/unready feeds. Record image quality/alarms; incomplete≠clear. Pending/alarm/missing-record requires examination, not make-up; prohibit blocked-chute release. Authorized-only chute access; staff retain alarmed bags until authorized disposition; normal return requires consistent ID/outcome/authorization. Explosives Response Team (Pebble) handles escalations with airport security personnel. Isolation: secure area/notify Baggage Operations Supervisor, who coordinates readiness/staffing/lane decisions/recovery with Security Duty Manager/Maintenance

New part:
S088: A scan mismatch prevents the bag from continuing on a route that depends on the unresolved identity.
S089: Congestion awareness uses current lane availability, conveyor stops, and the observed rate of incoming bags.
S090: The Baggage Operations Supervisor sets local congestion thresholds and confirms the authorized response to sustained overload.
S091: Tern is the operational alias used for the Baggage Operations Supervisor in sortation coordination.
S092: When a planned lane is unavailable, the Baggage Control System selects an approved alternate route only if screening status and flight timing remain valid.
S093: Bags with an unresolved destination or a route outside their handling limits are diverted to the Secondary Inspection Chute.
S094: The Image Resolution Desk resolves image-related holds before affected bags are returned to normal sortation.
S095: The Explosives Response Team manages security holds under the applicable response procedures.
S096: A bag returns to normal handling only after its identity, examination outcome, and routing authorization agree.
S097: The East Make-Up Conveyor and West Make-Up Conveyor are selected according to the active plan and available capacity.
S098: The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit operates within its assigned flight window and reports when its usable capacity is constrained.
S099: The Transfer Bag Feeder continues to hold transfer bags until screening status and intended onward handling are confirmed.
S100: The Bag Reconciliation Station compares bag identity with the active handling record and flags unresolved discrepancies.
S101: The Bag Reconciliation Station sends a Bag Match Query when bag identity cannot be reconciled with the active handling record.
S102: Bags found on a stopped or misdirected path are held from onward movement until their location and identity are established.
S103: The Maintenance Technician isolates a failed conveyor section and confirms that the route is safe before service resumes.
S104: The Baggage Operations Supervisor authorizes recovery to the approved sort plan after the cause of the abnormal path has been addressed.
S105: Flight Data Gateway maintains scheduled flight identifiers, destinations, planned departure times, and revisions needed for baggage planning.
S106: Flight schedules include airline-specific dispatch targets and connection windows, and changes are time-stamped for operational use.
S107: Baggage Control System evaluates flight assignments against current schedule data before accepting bag routing instructions.
S108: The planned dispatch time is the reference for prioritizing bags, while the published departure time remains the passenger-facing schedule value.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
